questions.stem: Which characteristic distinguishes hardware from software according to tangibility?

questions.explanation: The lecture states that software typically resides and operates within the hardware.

questions.stem: In what form do computers fundamentally process numerical data?
questions.explanation: The note explains that computers process numerical data in binary digital format.

questions.stem: How does machine language fundamentally differ from human-readable languages?

options.A: It uses symbols instead of numbers
options.C: It is based on binary representation

questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts machine language with human-readable languages by emphasizing its binary nature.

questions.stem: Depending on software capability, computers are especially effective at handling which type of tasks?
questions.explanation: The note highlights computers' ability to solve repetitive computational jobs efficiently.

questions.stem: Which combination best describes the performance of computers on repetitive computational tasks?
questions.explanation: The lecture specifies high accuracy and timeliness as key advantages.

questions.stem: What additional element, beyond hardware and software, is included in the definition of a computer system?
questions.explanation: A computer system is defined as hardware, software, and the users who operate it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a computer system according to the lecture?

options.C: A suite of hardware, software, and users

questions.stem: Which component is NOT listed as part of a full-fledged computer system?

questions.explanation: Each part of the computer system is explicitly called a subsystem.

questions.stem: Which unit of measurement is used to express CPU clock speed?

questions.stem: Which subsystem is identified as the main focus of the CSC 115 course?

questions.stem: Why is the hardware subsystem described as the bedrock of other subsystems?

options.A: It is optional in a computer system

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a characteristic of a computer?

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes hardware from software?

options.A: Hardware is intangible while software is physical
options.B: Software provides instructions while hardware executes them
options.D: Software wears out over time like hardware

questions.stem: Which item is an example of computer software?

questions.stem: Which item is classified as computer hardware?

questions.stem: Which classification criterion groups computers based on physical size?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly lists classification by size.

questions.stem: Personal computers are best described as which type of systems?
questions.explanation: PCs are defined as single-user computers based on microprocessors.

questions.stem: Who is credited with inventing the first runner of digital programmable and general-purpose computers in 1833?
questions.explanation: The lecture notes state that Charles Babbage invented the first runner of digital programmable and general-purpose computers in 1833.

questions.stem: ENIAC is historically significant primarily because it was the first:

questions.stem: The historical advancement of computer hardware is divided into generations mainly based on:
questions.explanation: The generations are partitioned according to specific ranges of improvements in hardware technology.

questions.stem: Which switching technology characterized first-generation computers?

questions.stem: A major drawback of first-generation computers was:
questions.explanation: The notes list slower speed, excessive heat, and high cost as drawbacks.

questions.stem: Which programming language format was primarily used in second-generation computers?
questions.explanation: Second-generation computers used assembly languages for programming.

questions.stem: What technological innovation made second-generation computers smaller and more energy-efficient?
questions.explanation: Transistors replaced vacuum tubes, making computers smaller, faster, and energy-efficient.

questions.stem: Integrated circuits were introduced as switching devices in which computer generation?
questions.explanation: The third generation introduced integrated circuits (ICs).

questions.stem: A key advantage of integrated circuits is that they:

options.B: Integrate multiple electronic components on a single chip

questions.explanation: ICs contain several transistors, capacitors, and resistors in one circuitry.

questions.stem: High-level programming languages were first introduced during which generation?
questions.explanation: The lecture notes state that high-level languages were introduced in the third generation.

questions.stem: Fourth-generation computers became widespread mainly due to the invention of:

questions.stem: Which technology enabled the design of microprocessors in fourth-generation computers?

questions.stem: Which company is credited as the first to design and develop microprocessors?

questions.stem: Fifth-generation computers are most strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: Fifth-generation computers incorporate AI, multi-core technology, and advanced integration.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a fifth-generation computing device?

questions.stem: Robots in the fifth generation are mainly designed to:

options.B: Support or replace humans in challenging environments

questions.stem: Computer software can best be described as:

options.B: Electrical wiring inside a system unit
options.C: A set of codes and instructions for executing tasks

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between hardware and software?

options.A: Hardware can function independently without software

questions.stem: Which category of software acts as an interface between users, hardware, and applications?
questions.explanation: The operating system interfaces between hardware, application software, and users.

questions.stem: Which operating system resource management function is NOT mentioned in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Compiler optimization is not listed among OS resource management responsibilities.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of input devices in a computer system?

options.A: To display processed data to users
options.C: To enable users to enter data and control parameters into the computer
options.D: To regulate power supply to the system unit

questions.explanation: Input devices allow users to enter data and control parameters which are later processed by the CPU.

questions.stem: After data is entered through an input device, it is first:
questions.explanation: Input data must be translated into a computer-readable form before processing by the CPU.

questions.stem: Which category of input devices is primarily used to move a cursor on the screen?

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT classified as a pointing input device?
questions.explanation: Scanners fall under scanning input devices, not pointing devices.

questions.stem: Optical Mark Recognition (OMR) belongs to which category of input devices?
questions.explanation: OMR is a scanning input device used to detect marks on paper.

questions.stem: Barcode readers are commonly used in supermarkets mainly to:
questions.explanation: Barcode readers decode barcodes to retrieve product data during sales.

questions.stem: Which device is regarded as the primary and most commonly used data entry device?

questions.stem: How many keys are typically found on a standard computer keyboard?

questions.stem: Which connection method allows a keyboard to operate without physical cables?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth enables wireless communication between the keyboard and system unit.

questions.stem: Which keys are specifically used for moving the cursor and controlling screen navigation?
questions.explanation: Cursor and screen control keys include arrow keys, page up, and page down.

questions.stem: A mouse controls cursor movement primarily through:

questions.stem: Which mouse buttons can be customized to perform different operations?
questions.explanation: The lecture note states that all three mouse buttons can be customized.

questions.stem: The primary function of an image scanner is to:

options.B: Convert printed materials into digital format

questions.stem: A trackball differs from a mouse because it:

options.C: Remains stationary while the ball is rotated

questions.stem: A light pen is best described as:
questions.explanation: A light pen detects light from the screen to enable pointing or drawing.

questions.stem: Headsets and microphones are categorized as input devices because they:

questions.stem: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology is mainly used to:

options.C: Convert printed text into machine-encoded text

questions.explanation: OCR converts printed or handwritten text into digital, machine-readable form.

questions.stem: A barcode reader decodes information by translating:
questions.explanation: Barcode readers convert reflected light into electrical signals for decoding.

questions.stem: Which statement best differentiates input devices from output devices?

options.B: Output devices send data to the computer
options.C: Input devices send data to the computer while output devices receive data from it

questions.explanation: This is the fundamental distinction stated in the lecture note.

questions.stem: Which output device is considered the primary means of displaying information?

questions.stem: Monitor resolution is determined mainly by the:
questions.explanation: Higher pixel count results in higher resolution and better image clarity.

questions.stem: Flat-panel monitors are preferred over CRT monitors mainly because they are:

questions.stem: Which flat-panel display type is described as non-emissive?
questions.explanation: LCD monitors are classified as non-emissive displays.

questions.stem: Laser printers differ from inkjet printers because laser printers:

options.B: Use powdered ink and laser technology

questions.stem: Impact printers produce output by:

questions.stem: Which output device is best suited for large architectural drawings?

questions.stem: Computer speakers receive audio signals through the:

questions.stem: The motherboard is best described as:

options.C: The main circuit board that interconnects system components

questions.stem: The chipset on a motherboard primarily controls:

options.B: Data flow between CPU, memory, and peripherals

questions.explanation: The chipset manages communication between major system components.

questions.stem: The CMOS battery on the motherboard is responsible for maintaining:
questions.explanation: The CMOS battery preserves system time and configuration data.

questions.stem: An increase in system clock pulses directly results in:
questions.explanation: More clock pulses per second allow the CPU to execute instructions faster.

questions.stem: Computer communication ports primarily serve as:

questions.stem: Which port technology allows plug-and-play connection of multiple devices?
questions.explanation: USB supports hot-plugging and multiple device connections.

questions.stem: The main difference between serial and parallel ports is that:

options.B: Parallel ports transmit data one bit at a time
options.C: Serial ports transmit one bit at a time
options.D: Parallel ports are faster than USB

questions.explanation: Serial ports send data sequentially, while parallel ports send multiple bits simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which statement best defines a computer according to the lecture note?

options.A: An electronic device that only performs arithmetic calculations

options.D: A programmable device that only accepts numerical input

questions.explanation: The note defines a computer as an electronic device capable of input, processing, output, and storage.

questions.stem: Why is software described as intangible?

options.B: Because it exists independently of hardware

questions.stem: In what form do computers fundamentally process data?

questions.stem: Which capability allows computers to solve repetitive computational jobs efficiently?

options.A: Only the hardware components of a computer

options.C: Because other subsystems depend on it to function

options.B: Hardware provides instructions while software executes them

questions.stem: Which classification groups computers based on processing power and physical size?

questions.stem: Which feature best describes personal computers (PCs)?

questions.stem: Why do laptops generally consume less power than desktop PCs?

questions.stem: Which type of computer is more powerful than a PC but still single-user?
questions.explanation: Workstations are single-user computers with higher specifications than PCs.

questions.stem: Minicomputers are best characterized as:
questions.explanation: The note states that minicomputers support multiple users simultaneously.

questions.stem: Which feature distinguishes mainframe computers from minicomputers?

options.B: Support for thousands of users simultaneously

questions.explanation: Mainframes support far more users concurrently than minicomputers.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes supercomputers?

options.A: They are smaller versions of mainframes
options.B: They are designed for routine office tasks
options.C: They perform extremely high-speed, data-intensive computations
options.D: They are mainly used for word processing

questions.explanation: Supercomputers are built to solve grand challenge, computation-intensive problems.

questions.stem: Which technological advancement enabled modern supercomputers to exist?
questions.explanation: The note links supercomputer capabilities to improvements in chip technology.

questions.stem: A microchip is best described as:

options.B: A set of electronic circuits etched on silicon
options.C: A storage medium made from plastic

questions.explanation: The lecture defines microchips as electronic circuits mounted on silicon slabs.

questions.stem: Why is silicon preferred over metals in chip manufacturing?

options.D: Silicon conducts electricity better than copper

questions.explanation: As a semiconductor, silicon’s conductivity can be modified, unlike metals.

questions.stem: What does Moore’s Law primarily predict?

options.B: The cost of computers halves every year
options.C: The number of transistors on a chip doubles about every two years
options.D: Memory capacity remains constant over time

questions.explanation: Moore’s Law forecasts the doubling of transistor density approximately every two years.

questions.stem: Which outcome is a direct implication of Moore’s Law?
questions.explanation: The law implies smaller transistors and more powerful, compact chips.

questions.stem: Which future chip technology is expected to succeed transistor miniaturization?
questions.explanation: The note states future designs will rely on parallelism, 3D, and multi-core technologies.

questions.stem: Why is regular computer maintenance important?

options.C: To extend device lifespan and ensure optimal performance

questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes maintenance for efficiency, longevity, and reliability.

questions.stem: Which description best defines a computer network?

options.A: A single computer connected to peripheral devices
options.B: A system of interconnected computers and hardware for sharing data and resources
options.C: A collection of software programs running on one machine
options.D: A wireless communication system used only for Internet access

questions.explanation: A computer network is defined as multiple computers and computing hardware interconnected to share data, information, and resources.

questions.stem: In a computer network, what role does a server primarily play?

options.A: It converts analog signals to digital signals
options.B: It stores files and resources that can be accessed by other computers
options.D: It acts as a gateway between wireless networks

questions.explanation: The note explains that files and documents can be created, saved, and stored on a server and accessed by other computers on the network.

questions.stem: What term is used to describe computers connected on a network?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that computers on a network are called nodes or hosts.

questions.stem: Why must multiple wired or wireless paths in a network be carefully designed?

options.A: To reduce the cost of network devices
options.B: To enable reliable sending and receiving of data
options.C: To eliminate the need for network protocols
options.D: To increase the physical size of the network

questions.explanation: The note emphasizes that paths must be carefully designed to enable sending and receiving data as required.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is primarily responsible for directing data between networks?
questions.explanation: Routers are listed as network-enabled equipment that support communication over long ranges by directing data between networks.

questions.stem: Which key difference distinguishes a modem from a network card?

options.A: A modem sends data over a network cable, while a network card uses phone lines
options.B: A modem sends information over a communication line, while a network card sends over a network cable
options.C: A modem is used only in LANs, while a network card is used only in WANs
options.D: A modem is faster and more reliable than a network card

questions.explanation: The lecture directly compares their roles, highlighting the transmission medium used by each.

questions.stem: Which limitation of modems is identified in the lecture note?

options.B: Susceptibility to phone line static and slower speed

questions.explanation: The note states that modems are usually slow and susceptible to problems such as phone line static.

questions.stem: Which component allows a computer to connect to a LAN or ISP through a cable modem or DSL?
questions.explanation: The lecture explains that network cards connect computers to LANs or ISPs via cable modem or DSL.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a basic requirement of a computer network?
questions.explanation: The note lists network software, protocols, transmission media, devices, and multiple computers, not application software alone.

questions.stem: Which cable type is identified as the most commonly used network communication medium?
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that ethernet cables are the most commonly used network cables.

questions.stem: Which connector is commonly associated with Category 5 and Category 6 Ethernet cables?
questions.explanation: The note specifies that CAT 5 and CAT 6 Ethernet cables use RJ-45 connectors.

questions.stem: Which type of network is designed for data transmission among personal devices using Bluetooth or Wi-Fi?

questions.stem: Which network type interconnects computers within a limited geographical area such as a school or office?
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) connects computers within a local place or area.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) from a traditional LAN?

options.B: It integrates two or more LANs into a shared segment

questions.explanation: A VLAN involves two or more LANs configured and integrated to share resources.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly characterizes a Wide Area Network (WAN)?

options.A: It connects devices within a single room
options.B: It extends over a large geographical region using leased circuits
options.C: It is limited to personal devices

questions.explanation: WANs extend over large geographical regions and are often established with leased telecommunication circuits.

questions.stem: Why is the Internet considered a WAN?

options.A: Because it connects only private networks
options.B: Because it is restricted to academic institutions
options.C: Because it spans large geographical areas and connects many networks
options.D: Because it uses only wireless technology

questions.explanation: The Internet is described as a worldwide interconnection of many network types, fitting the definition of a WAN.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of a Storage Area Network (SAN)?
questions.explanation: SANs provide access to large integrated arrays or block-level data storage.

questions.stem: What feature allows users of a WLAN to remain connected while moving within a coverage area?
questions.explanation: WLANs use high-frequency radio waves, enabling mobility within the coverage area.

questions.stem: Which characteristic best defines an intranet?
questions.explanation: An intranet is a dedicated and classified network strictly within an organization.

questions.stem: How does an extranet differ from an intranet?

options.B: It allows controlled access to authorized external parties

questions.explanation: An extranet permits access to specific authorized external bodies without exposing the entire network.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?

options.B: To extend a private network over a public network securely

questions.explanation: A VPN enables users to send and receive data over public networks as if directly connected to a private network.

questions.stem: What defines a peer-to-peer (P2P) network?
questions.explanation: In P2P networks, peers are equally privileged and share workloads.

questions.stem: Which type of maintenance is performed to prevent hardware failures before they occur?
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance is done proactively to avoid hardware failures.

questions.stem: Corrective maintenance is primarily performed when:
questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance addresses hardware faults after they occur.

questions.stem: Predictive maintenance aims to:

options.B: Predict potential hardware failures before they happen

questions.explanation: Predictive maintenance uses monitoring to anticipate failures.

questions.stem: Which tools are commonly used for computer hardware maintenance?

options.A: Anti-static wrist strap, screwdrivers, compressed air

questions.explanation: These are standard tools for safely maintaining and cleaning computer hardware.

questions.stem: Why is it important to use an anti-static wrist strap when handling computer components?

options.B: To prevent electrostatic discharge that can damage components

questions.explanation: Static electricity can destroy sensitive hardware parts, and wrist straps prevent this.

questions.stem: Which environmental factor is critical to maintaining computer hardware?
questions.explanation: High temperature or humidity can damage hardware; proper environmental control is essential.

questions.stem: What is a common sign that a hardware component might be failing?

options.B: Unexpected shutdowns, strange noises, or performance slowdown

questions.explanation: These symptoms often indicate hardware issues.

questions.stem: Which practice ensures the safe backup and storage of computer data?

options.B: Using cloud storage and external drives regularly

questions.explanation: Regular backups on reliable media prevent data loss during hardware failures.

questions.stem: Why is regular cleaning of dust from computer hardware important?

options.B: Prevents overheating and prolongs component life

questions.explanation: Dust can block airflow and cause overheating, leading to hardware damage.
